current_bottleneck: The one-shot joint path velocity must know the implied future level/state path to model state-dependent drift and mean reversion. 304a gives the velocity transition tokens plus history context only, so cumulative level state is implicit and hard to recover; recursive 303b exposes current logit state directly and preserves MR/correlation better.
last_result_summary: Postmortem compared 303b, 303d, 301a/302a, and 304a. 303b scores 4/11 with corr ratio 0.911 and MR h30 0.832 because each transition velocity sees current_logit. 303d forces MR but collapses coverage. 304a scores 1/11 with MR near zero and corr ratio 0.466. 301a also has near-zero MR, while 302a's implied-state exposure improves MR but remains weak.
next_step_recommendation: Run 304b as the minimal causal repair: keep the one-shot joint token flow, but expose per-token implied state logits computed from the current noisy transition tensor and the last history logit. This is a coordinate/Markov-state exposure, not a new side path or evaluator-specific knob.
